To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the firm is a nexus of specific contracts; (2) the firm exists to reduce the costs of using the price mechanism, and (3) the firm is an organization to minimize transaction costs.11 In their paper, Jensen and Mecklin adopted the Alchian-Demsetz definition of the firm and extended the Alchian and Demsetz conception to the corporation.12 The firm, they argued, is not a unit of production, but rather a set of contracts

(1) the firm is a nexus of contractual relationships, (2) the firm's boundaries are determined by the costs of organizing transactions within the firm relative to the costs of using the price mechanism to organize the same transactions, (3) the firm is not an entity separate from and distinct from the individuals composing it; it is merely a shorthand reference to a particular nexus of contracts, (4) the firm's existence, as such, is dependent upon the transactions costs of using the prices mechanism

(a) the firm is a nexus of contractual relationships, (b) the contractual relationships are between individuals and the firm, not between individuals per se, and (c) the firm's contractual relationships with individuals are not the same as the relationships between individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and extent of economic activities which are not organized as market transactions.
the organization of productive activity, and the economic forces that influence its organization.
the organization of production, not with the organization of firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a firm is an organization of production in which the participants are jointly and severally responsible, in the sense of being subject to sanctions, for all of the productive services that they contribute.
the firm is a nexus of agreements, the content of which is to be decided by the parties themselves.
the firm is an organization of production, and that the firm is a nexus of specific contractual relations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the firm is a nexus of contracting relationships.11 The firm is a nexus because it consists of a network of contracts.12 The firm is a set of contracts because it is the result of a series of contracting relationships.13 The firm is a contract because it is an agreement.14 The firm is a network because it is a series of agreements, and because the agreements are connected to one another.15 The firm is a series of contracts because it consists of contracts between the firm and its employees,

a firm is a nexus of specific human relationships that have evolved because they have been found to be useful by their participants.11 The participants in the nexus are the individuals who contribute to the production of goods and services.12 The participants are linked by contracts that specify their respective contributions.13 The nexus, in other words, is a nexus of contractual relations.
the Coasian entrepreneur-coordinator is not necessary for the existence of the firm.11 The firm is not a nexus of contracts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the firm is a nexus of contractual relations among individuals, and not a production function in the sense of neoclassical economics, which assumes that a firm is a production function.11 In this conception, the firm is not defined by the direction of the price mechanism, but by the direction of a contract.
the firm is a nexus of contractual relations.
the Coasean conception is incomplete.
